draft.text: You came in because you have low back pain that started two weeks ago after lifting a box of books and feeling a pop.
The pain is achy and sharp, and it has gotten worse over time.
Sometimes the pain shoots down your left leg, but you have not had numbness, tingling, or weakness in your leg.
We did not find any results from tests or exams during this visit.
You have not had imaging studies, physical therapy, or neurological tests for this condition yet.
Your pain may be related to your lower back, and it may involve a nerve root.
You are unsure if you need more tests to check for nerve issues.
The doctor mentioned the possibility of an MRI to look at the cause of your back pain.
The next steps will be discussed.
